easy.def: A word you say when something hurts.
examples: Ouch! That hurt.
I said ouch.
Ouch, I stubbed my toe.

more.def: A word that you shout when you feel a sudden pain.
examples: Ouch, that stove is hot!
She yelled ouch when the bee stung her.
"Ouch!" he said as he stubbed his toe.

easy.def: Used to say what is the right thing to do.
examples: You ought to wear a helmet.
We ought to say thank you.
You ought to rest.

more.def: Used to say that something is right, wise or likely.
examples: You ought to wear a coat in this weather.
We ought to arrive before dark.
She ought to be home by now.

easy.def: A small unit of weight.
examples: The apple weighs five ounces.
An ounce is small.
I need an ounce.

more.def: A unit for measuring weight, equal to one sixteenth of a pound.
examples: The apple weighed six ounces.
There are sixteen ounces in a pound.
Add an ounce of cheese.

easy.def: A word that shows something belongs to us.
examples: This is our house.
Our dog is silly.
We love our school.

more.def: A word used to show that something belongs to or is connected with the speaker and others.
examples: Our class is going on a trip to the farm.
We picked apples from our own tree.
Our team practices every Tuesday after school.

easy.def: Belonging to us.
examples: The red house is ours.
This ball is ours.
That dog is ours.

more.def: The one or ones that belong to us.
examples: The blue bikes are ours.
This table is ours.
Your house is big, but ours is small.

easy.def: We, and not someone else.
examples: We made lunch ourselves.
We hurt ourselves.
We looked at ourselves in the mirror.

more.def: Used when "we" are the ones who do something and also receive it.
examples: We built the fort by ourselves.
We taught ourselves to juggle.
We saw ourselves in the video.

easy.def: Away from the inside of a place.
examples: The dog ran out.
Let us go out to play.
He took out his book.

more.def: Away from the inside of a place, or not at home or at work.
examples: The children ran out into the yard as soon as the rain stopped.
Mom is out shopping, but she will be back soon.
The turtle stuck its head out of its shell.

easy.def: A time when power or water stops.
examples: A power outage happened.
The outage was long.
There was an outage.

more.def: A period when power or another service stops working.
examples: A power outage left the town in the dark.
The outage lasted three hours.
We lit candles during the outage.

easy.def: The dry, empty land in the middle of Australia.
examples: He lives in the outback.
The outback is dry.
Kangaroos live in the outback.

more.def: The wide, dry, empty land in the middle of Australia.
examples: Kangaroos live in the Australian outback.
The outback is hot and dry.
A farmer lives far out in the outback.

easy.def: A motor fixed to the back of a small boat.
examples: The boat has an outboard.
The outboard is loud.
He started the outboard.

more.def: A motor that is fixed to the back of a small boat, outside the hull.
examples: The fisherman started the outboard and headed out.
The outboard pushed the little boat across the lake.
He tilted the outboard out of the water.

easy.def: A sudden start of something bad, like a sickness.
examples: There was an outbreak of flu.
An outbreak of fire.
The outbreak was small.

more.def: A sudden start of something bad, such as a sickness or a fire.
examples: There was an outbreak of flu at the school, so many kids stayed home.
Firefighters stopped the outbreak of the fire quickly.
An outbreak of loud laughter filled the room.

easy.def: A small building near a main house.
examples: The tools are in the outbuilding.
An outbuilding is a shed.
The outbuilding is small.

more.def: A small building separate from the main house, such as a shed or barn.
examples: The farmer kept tools in an outbuilding.
There were three outbuildings on the farm.
The outbuilding stood near the garden.

easy.def: A sudden loud show of strong feeling.
examples: He had an outburst of laughter.
An angry outburst.
The outburst surprised us.

more.def: A sudden, strong release of a feeling such as anger or laughter, often in a loud way.
examples: The funny joke caused an outburst of laughter in the class.
His angry outburst surprised everyone.
There was an outburst of cheering when the team scored.

easy.def: A person who is left out by others.
examples: He felt like an outcast.
The outcast sat alone.
Nobody wants to be an outcast.

more.def: A person who is pushed out of a group or not accepted by others.
examples: The new boy felt like an outcast until someone invited him to play.
In the story, the girl was an outcast who found a friend in the forest.
No one should be made to feel like an outcast.

easy.def: What happens in the end.
examples: The game ended in a tie.
We liked the outcome.
The outcome was a surprise.

more.def: The result of something, or how it turns out.
examples: The outcome of the game was a tie.
We waited to hear the outcome of the vote.
The outcome of the experiment surprised the scientists.

easy.def: A loud cry of anger or alarm from many people.
examples: There was an outcry.
The outcry was loud.
People made an outcry.

more.def: A strong and loud protest by many people.
examples: There was an outcry when the park was closed.
The crowd raised an outcry against the unfair rule.
The outcry made the mayor change his mind.

easy.def: Old and not used anymore.
examples: The map is outdated.
An outdated phone.
The outdated rule was dropped.

more.def: No longer in use because newer ones are better.
examples: The outdated map did not show the new road.
His outdated phone could not run the new game.
The outdated textbook still said Pluto was a planet.

easy.def: To do better than someone else.
examples: She outdid her brother.
He tried to outdo me.
Try to outdo yourself.

more.def: To do better than someone else or than you did before.
examples: She outdid herself by baking three cakes for the party.
The two brothers always try to outdo each other.
He outdid all the other runners and won the race.

easy.def: Done or used outside.
examples: We play outdoor games.
An outdoor pool.
The outdoor market.

more.def: Done, used or found outside, not inside a building.
examples: We play outdoor games at recess when the weather is nice.
The hotel has an outdoor pool.
An outdoor market sells fresh fruit every Saturday.

easy.def: Outside, not in a building.
examples: We like to play outdoors.
The dog sleeps outdoors.
It is cold outdoors today.

more.def: Outside, in the open air.
examples: On sunny days, our class eats lunch outdoors.
The concert was held outdoors in the park.
He loves working outdoors on the farm.

easy.def: On the outside.
examples: The outer layer is thick.
The outer wall is brick.
Space is outer.

more.def: Farther from the middle, on the outside.
examples: The outer layer of the onion is dry.
We walked along the outer wall of the castle.
Pluto is in the outer part of the solar system.

easy.def: The farthest out.
examples: The outermost ring.
The outermost layer.
The outermost shelf.

more.def: Farthest from the center or the inside.
examples: The outermost ring of the target was white.
She wore a coat as her outermost layer.
The outermost island was tiny.

easy.def: The far part of a baseball field.
examples: He plays outfield.
The ball flew to the outfield.
The outfield is grass.

more.def: The part of a baseball field that is farthest from home plate.
examples: He plays in the outfield.
The ball sailed deep into the outfield.
The outfield was green and wide.

easy.def: A set of clothes worn together.
examples: She wore a new outfit.
My outfit is blue.
He chose an outfit.

more.def: A set of clothes that you wear together.
examples: She wore a blue outfit to the party.
He picked a warm outfit for the snow.
The clown's outfit was bright and silly.

easy.def: Friendly and likes to meet people.
examples: She is outgoing.
An outgoing child.
He has an outgoing nature.

more.def: Friendly and cheerful, and enjoying meeting and talking with other people.
examples: She is an outgoing girl who makes friends quickly.
The outgoing puppy greeted everyone at the park.
He has an outgoing nature and loves to talk.

easy.def: To get too big for something.
examples: I outgrow my shoes fast.
He outgrew his coat.
She will outgrow the bed.

more.def: To grow too big for something, or to stop liking something as you get older.
examples: Babies outgrow their clothes quickly.
She outgrew her old bike last year.
He outgrew his fear of the dark.

easy.def: A short trip for fun.
examples: We went on an outing.
The outing was fun.
Our class had an outing.

more.def: A short trip taken for fun or pleasure.
examples: Our class went on an outing to the zoo.
We packed lunch for the family outing.
The outing to the park was a lot of fun.

easy.def: Very strange and odd.
examples: She wore an outlandish hat.
An outlandish costume.
The outlandish idea.

more.def: Strange and unusual, in a way that seems odd.
examples: She wore an outlandish hat with feathers and bells.
The outlandish costume made everyone laugh.
He had an outlandish plan to fly with balloons.

easy.def: To last longer than.
examples: The battery will outlast the toy.
The old chair outlasted the new.
Stone outlasts wood.

more.def: To last longer than something else.
examples: The old chair will outlast the new one.
Stone houses outlast wooden ones.
The runner outlasted everyone in the race.

easy.def: A place on the wall where you plug in things.
examples: Plug it in the outlet.
The outlet is on the wall.
Do not touch the outlet.

more.def: A place on a wall where you plug in a lamp or machine, or an opening where water or air flows out.
examples: Plug the lamp into the outlet beside the desk.
Water flows out of the lake through a narrow outlet.
Never put anything but a plug into an electrical outlet.

easy.def: A line that shows the outside edge of something.
examples: I drew an outline of a cat.
The outline is black.
I saw the outline of the hill.

more.def: A line that shows the shape or outer edge of something.
examples: I drew an outline of my hand.
The outline of the mountain was dark against the sky.
She colored in the outline of a butterfly.

easy.def: A short plan of what you will write.
examples: I made an outline of my story.
The teacher checked the outline.
We write an outline.

more.def: A short plan that lists the main points of something that you are going to write or say.
examples: I made an outline for my report before writing.
The teacher checked our outline for each essay.
An outline helps you organize your ideas.

easy.def: To draw the edge of something or tell the main points.
examples: I outline my hand.
She outlined the plan.
He outlined the story.

more.def: To draw the outer edge of something, or to give the main points of it.
examples: I outlined my hand on the paper.
She outlined her plan for the class project.
The teacher outlined the rules of the game.

easy.def: To live longer than someone.
examples: Turtles outlive many animals.
She outlived her brothers.
Trees can outlive people.

more.def: To live longer than another person or thing, or to last longer than something.
examples: Giant tortoises can outlive people by many years.
The old oak tree outlived everyone who planted it.
The song outlived the band that made it.

easy.def: The way you think about things.
examples: She has a happy outlook.
A bright outlook.
The outlook is good.

more.def: The way you look at the world or the future, or what is likely to happen.
examples: She has a cheerful outlook and always sees the bright side.
The weather outlook for the weekend is sunny.
With a good outlook, hard tasks seem easier.

easy.def: To be more than something else.
examples: Girls outnumber boys here.
The ants outnumbered us.
Stars outnumber planets.

more.def: To be greater in number than another group.
examples: Girls outnumber boys in our class.
The ants outnumbered the crumbs.
Stars far outnumber the planets we see.

easy.def: A small camp or town far from other places.
examples: The outpost was far away.
An outpost in the desert.
The outpost had a flag.

more.def: A small camp or settlement far from the main place.
examples: The outpost stood alone on the frozen plain.
The explorers reached a remote outpost.
A trading outpost sat on the river.

easy.def: A flood of something.
examples: An outpouring of love.
The outpouring of support.
An outpouring of water.

more.def: A big rush of feeling or words.
examples: There was an outpouring of love for the town.
The outpouring of help surprised us.
An outpouring of water filled the road.

easy.def: The amount that something makes.
examples: The factory has a big output.
The farm's output was corn.
The machine's output went up.

more.def: The amount of something that a person, machine or place makes.
examples: The factory's output doubled in a year.
The farm's output of milk was highest in spring.
A computer shows its output on the screen.

easy.def: A very strong, angry feeling about something not fair.
examples: The class felt outrage at the unfair rule.
He spoke with outrage.
There was outrage when the park closed.

more.def: A powerful feeling of anger caused by something that seems very wrong or unfair.
examples: The town felt outrage when someone cut down the old oak tree.
Her face showed outrage when she saw the litter in the river.
Neighbors spoke of their outrage at the plan to close the library.

easy.def: To make someone very angry about something not fair.
examples: The mean trick outraged us.
The broken swing outraged the kids.
Cruel words outrage me.

more.def: To make someone feel very angry because something seems unfair or very wrong.
examples: Dumping trash in the stream outraged the people who lived nearby.
The unfair call outraged the fans, and they booed loudly.
It outraged her that the pond was filled with litter.

easy.def: Very, very angry because something is not fair.
examples: He was outraged by the rule.
The crowd was outraged.
She felt outraged.

more.def: Extremely angry because something seems wrong or unfair.
examples: The fans were outraged by the unfair call.
She was outraged when someone broke her project.
The neighbors were outraged by the loud noise at night.

easy.def: Shocking and very bad or unusual.
examples: The price was outrageous.
He wore an outrageous hat.
An outrageous idea.

more.def: So unusual or extreme that it shocks people.
examples: The price of the toy was outrageous.
He wore an outrageous hat with feathers.
That is an outrageous story.

easy.def: To be higher than someone else.
examples: A captain outranks a sergeant.
The general outranked him.
She outranks him.

more.def: To have a higher rank or position than someone else.
examples: A captain outranks a lieutenant.
The queen outranks all the other nobles.
He outranked everyone in the club.

easy.def: Reaching out to help others.
examples: The school did outreach.
Outreach helps.
The club does outreach.

more.def: An effort to reach out and offer help or information to people.
examples: The library does outreach to families.
The club's outreach brought food to neighbors.
Outreach programs help those in need.

easy.def: A float on the side of a small boat.
examples: The canoe has an outrigger.
The outrigger keeps it steady.
An outrigger floats.

more.def: A float attached to the side of a boat by poles that keeps it from tipping.
examples: The canoe had an outrigger to keep it steady.
Islanders paddled the outrigger across the lagoon.
The outrigger floated on the waves.

easy.def: Completely and openly.
examples: He said no outright.
She laughed outright.
They won outright.

more.def: Completely and directly, with nothing held back.
examples: He refused outright to go.
She laughed outright at the joke.
The team won the cup outright.

easy.def: Complete and clear.
examples: It was an outright win.
He gave an outright no.
An outright lie.

more.def: Total and clear, with no doubt.
examples: It was an outright victory for our team.
She told an outright lie, and it was easy to see.
The test was an outright disaster.

easy.def: To run faster than someone.
examples: The rabbit outran the fox.
I outran my friend.
She can outrun everyone.

more.def: To run faster or farther than someone or something.
examples: The rabbit outran the fox and hid in its burrow.
She can outrun everyone in her class.
The cheetah can outrun almost any animal.

easy.def: The beginning.
examples: From the outset.
At the outset of the trip.
He knew from the outset.

more.def: The start or beginning of something.
examples: From the outset, we knew it would be fun.
At the outset of the race, he was behind.
She knew from the outset that she would win.

easy.def: To shine brighter than someone else.
examples: The sun outshone the stars.
She outshone the others.
The star outshines the moon.

more.def: To shine brighter than others, or to do better than others.
examples: The sun outshines all the other stars.
She outshone the others at the talent show.
The bright lamp outshone the candle.

easy.def: Not in a house or building.
examples: Let's play outside.
The dog is outside.
It is cold outside.

more.def: In the open air, not in a building.
examples: We eat lunch outside when it is sunny.
The children ran outside as soon as the rain stopped.
It was warm outside, so we left the windows open.

easy.def: The outer part of something.
examples: The outside of the box is red.
I painted the outside of the house.
The outside of the nut is hard.

more.def: The outer surface or part of something.
examples: The outside of the cake was covered with frosting.
Wipe the outside of the cup with a towel.
The outside of the castle was made of gray stone.

easy.def: Not inside.
examples: Wait outside the door.
The dog sat outside the shop.
We played outside the school.

more.def: On the other side of the walls or door of a place.
examples: A crowd stood outside the museum waiting for it to open.
She left her muddy boots outside the front door.
The picnic tables are just outside the cafe.

easy.def: A person who is not part of a group.
examples: The new kid felt like an outsider.
I did not want to be an outsider.
An outsider joined our game.

more.def: A person who does not belong to a certain group or place.
examples: The new kid felt like an outsider on the first day.
We welcomed the outsider and asked her to join our game.
Outsiders were not allowed inside the club house.

easy.def: Larger than usual.
examples: An outsize coat.
The outsize box.
Outsize shoes.

more.def: Much bigger than usual.
examples: He wore an outsize coat.
The outsize box was hard to lift.
The clown wore outsize shoes.

easy.def: The edges of a town.
examples: We live on the outskirts.
The outskirts are quiet.
A farm on the outskirts of town.

more.def: The outer parts of a town or city.
examples: We live on the outskirts of the city.
A small farm was on the outskirts of town.
The outskirts are quieter than downtown.

easy.def: To win by being cleverer.
examples: The mouse outsmarted the cat.
I outsmarted my friend.
She outsmarted him.

more.def: To beat someone by being more clever than they are.
examples: The mouse outsmarted the cat and escaped through a tiny hole.
In the story, a clever girl outsmarted the wolf.
I outsmarted my brother in the game of chess.

easy.def: Saying what you think out loud.
examples: She is outspoken.
An outspoken girl.
He was outspoken.

more.def: Saying exactly what you think, even if others may not agree.
examples: She is outspoken and always shares her opinion.
The outspoken boy told the class what he thought.
He was outspoken about saving the park.

easy.def: Spread out wide.
examples: The bird had outspread wings.
His outspread arms.
The outspread map.

more.def: Stretched out or spread wide.
examples: The eagle soared with outspread wings.
She greeted him with outspread arms.
The outspread map covered the table.

easy.def: Very good.
examples: She did outstanding work.
The outstanding player won.
It was an outstanding show.

more.def: Much better than usual, excellent.
examples: She did outstanding work on her project.
The outstanding player won the award.
The show was outstanding from start to finish.

easy.def: Reached out.
examples: She ran with outstretched arms.
The outstretched hand waited.
He stood with outstretched wings.

more.def: Stretched out as far as possible.
examples: She ran to him with outstretched arms.
The bird glided with outstretched wings.
He waited with an outstretched hand.

easy.def: To go faster than another.
examples: The horse outstripped the rest.
She outstripped her friends.
He outstripped them.

more.def: To move faster than someone or something, or to do better than them.
examples: The fastest horse outstripped the others.
She soon outstripped her classmates in math.
Demand outstripped supply.

easy.def: Toward the outside.
examples: The gate swings outward.
The ripples spread outward.
He looked outward.

more.def: Away from the center, toward the outside.
examples: Ripples spread outward from where the stone landed.
The door opens outward.
The petals of the flower spread outward.

easy.def: On the outside; what you can see.
examples: Her outward calm hid her worry.
His outward smile.
The outward look.

more.def: Showing on the outside, such as how someone seems to others.
examples: Her outward calm hid how nervous she was.
The outward appearance of the house was neat.
He showed no outward sign of fear.

easy.def: On the outside.
examples: Outwardly, he was calm.
She looked calm outwardly.
He smiled outwardly.

more.def: On the outside, or in the way things seem.
examples: Outwardly he was calm, but inside he was nervous.
She looked outwardly happy.
The house looked outwardly neat.

easy.def: To be heavier or more important than.
examples: The elephant outweighs the horse.
The good outweighs the bad.
A truck outweighs a car.

more.def: To weigh more than something, or to be more important than something.
examples: An elephant outweighs a horse.
The good things outweighed the bad.
The benefits outweigh the cost.

easy.def: To trick someone by being smarter.
examples: The fox will outwit the dog.
She outwitted the cat.
He outwitted his friend.

more.def: To defeat someone by being cleverer or sneakier.
examples: The clever fox outwitted the hounds.
She outwitted her brother at chess.
The mouse outwitted the cat.
